SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:

families

the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE

Modernization of Meteorological
Department

BHARTIA:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of EARTH
SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government plans to
modernize the country's Meteorological
Department to be able to provide agriculture
related weather information which is crucial
for optimal agricultural production, to
farmers in all the 600 districts in the
country;
(b) if so, whether the entire process will
take about five-six years;
(c) if so, whether the system needs to
be modernized and the basic structure will
be ready by 2008;

(d) if so, the other plans for revamping
the Meteorological Department; and
(e) to what extent it will be more
modernized?
Upgradation of facilities in higher
education
*84. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Centre has written to
the States lagging in higher education with
a view to help them to upgrade these
facilities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what is the status of Orissa in the
higher education survey that has been
conducted for the purpose; and
(d) what is the action plan of
Government to help Orissa in the matter?
New Mining Policy
*85. SHRI DHARAM PAL SABHAR-
WAL: Will the Minister of MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
considering to put in place a New Mining
Policy;
(b) if so, the salient features of the
proposed policy;
(c) whether it is a fact that State
Governments are not granting mining lease
rights within the stipulated period; and
(d) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to make it mandatory for State
Governments to grant mining lease rights
within the stipulated period?
Vocational training
*86. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that our vocational
training lags far behind the rest of the world
and only 153 courses are recognised out of
2945 vocational courses offered round the
globe;
(b) if so, Government's response
thereto; and
(c) whether Government are seriously
considering to introduce career oriented new
specialized vocational courses for getting
more employment opportunities to the
youth in various parts of the country?
FDI in higher education
*87. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
permit FDI in higher education in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of recognized Central,
State, State-aided, private and deemed
universities currently operating in the
country, State-wise;
(d) whether certain sections of the
academics are opposed to FDI in education
sector on the ground that private and
Government aided universities would not
be able to compete with foreign universities
operating in the country; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto?

30

Vacancies in schools
†*88. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that various
categories of posts are lying vacant in
Government schools, Kendriya Vidyalayas
and Navodaya Vidyalayas in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons behind these vacancies; and
(c) the details of Government's plan to
fill up the said vacancies?
Mines leased to National Mineral
Development Corporation
*89. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
 Will the Minister of MINES be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of mines leased to
National Mineral Development
Corporation (NMDC);
(b) whether some of these mines are
due for renewal and the proposal for the
lease of fresh mines applied by NMDC is
pending with Government;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken to clear such mining
lease/renewal of applications?
NSSO report on education
*90. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether National Sample Survey
Organisation’s report on the status of
education and vocational training in India,
2004-05 found that over 50 per cent rural
households and 20 per cent urban
households do not have even one literate
woman in their families above the age of
15;
(b) whether the report is the third in the
series of seven reports to be brought out
on the basis of the survey and like all regular
NSSO surveys, the present survey covered
practically the whole of the Indian
population; and
(c) what are the other main points
mentioned in the report and whether
Government have taken these issues
seriously?
Teaching of different syllabus in
schools
*91. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether curricula are being prepared
and pursued independently by schools run
by various organizations, especially
religious organizations in the country;
(b) if so, the State-wise details of
number of such schools in the country;
(c) whether Government are aware that
factual errors and distortions are found in
the syllabi particularly in History being
taught in some of these schools;
(d) if so, whether Government have
evolved any mechanism to monitor the
situation;
(e) whether there is any proposal to
bring a uniform syllabus in schools across
the country; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?

31
Different electricity rates in NDMC
and MCD areas
*92. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are two
sets of rates of electricity in Delhi-one for
consumers living in NDMC areas and the
other for rest of Delhi, if so, the reasons for
the discriminatory rates; and
(b) whether Government propose to do
away with the discriminatory rates, if not,
the reasons therefor?
Assistance for welfare
of tribals
*93. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA:  Will the
Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased
to state the details of approvals and
financial assistance provided to the State
Governments during the last three years
and till-date for development and welfare
of the tribals in the country, State-wise and
year-wise?
Drop-out rate in Muslim
children
*94. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that majority of
the 13.5 million drop-out children are
Muslims;
(b) Government's reaction to this high
drop-out rate in Muslim children;
(c) whether it is a fact that 30 per cent
of all Muslim children in Bihar are out of
school totally; and
(d) if so, the steps proposed to remedy
this situation?
Suggestions on New Mining Policy
†*95. SHRI PYARELAL KHAN-
DELWAL: Will the Minister of MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
contemplating on formulating a New
Mining Policy;
(b) if so, by when the same would be
implemented;
(c) whether Government have received
any suggestions regarding royalty etc. in
the New Mining Policy from political
parties and other organizations of various
States;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the details of the action taken
thereon?
Proposal for Arctic expedition
 *96. SHRI DEVDAS APTE: Will the
Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning for the Arctic expedition to
research on the climate change with another
team;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the total budget allocation for this
purpose;
(d) the key areas on which this
expedition will concentrate; and
(e) by when India would be able to send
its first Arctic expedition on its own?
Mini Anganwadi Centres
*97. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Anganwadi Centres in the country;
(b) what are the services provided
through these Mini Anganwadi Centres; and

Anganwadi Centres are being paid the same
remuneration as the other Anganwadi
workers and helpers?
Committee constituted to check
ragging
†*98.SHRI SHATRUGHAN
SINHA:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
 Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether on the direction of Supreme
Court, Government have constituted any
Committee to suggest measures to check
incidents of ragging in educational
institutes;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the progress made so far in the
Committee's work;
(d) by when a suitable legislation is
proposed to be enacted in this regard;
(e) whether Government are in a
position to assure the Parliament that
considering ragging as a serious offence, it
will bring it to zero level; and

distribution of power

Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether under the Electricity Act
2003, whosoever is desirous of supplying
power can set up a power generation,
transmission and distribution system to
enable the demand for power to be met;
(b) if so, Government's action plan to
realise this scenario;
(c) the systemic hurdles that are not
allowing this situation from being realized;
and
(d) if the answer to part (a) be in
negative, the reasons therefor?
Utilisation of installed power capacity
*100. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of installed capacity,
project-wise and grid-wise as on 2006;
(b) the details of utilisation of installed
capacity;
(c) whether it is a fact that the country
is not in a position to utilise the installed
capacity to its full length in generation due
to age, seasonal fluctuations and fuel
constraints; and
(d) if so, the measures initiated by
Government to see that the installed
capacity may be fully utilised?

Committee?

10 different streams to make them more

Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
